The people

Thousands of lives. Live on your map.

Lifelike NPCs built from MetaHumans, each with a reason to be there, and you can talk to every one of them, inside the terminal and out. Your holographic map shows them all, floor by floor, and flashes the moment something happens.

  • Walk up to any NPC, in or outside the terminal, and talk to them
  • Every passenger has a booking, a mood, money and a trip to finish
  • Pilots, cabin crew, ground crew, security, police, cleaners and fire crews, each in a proper uniform
  • Incidents blink on the map: a difficult passenger, a guard escort, a lost bag
  • Staff work their shifts and drive home to the town afterwards
  • …and much more

The economy

Money in and money out.

Hiring people is only the start: every one of them needs a salary. Everything the airport uses has to be bought and paid for, and the money coming in has to cover it.

  • +Shop and restaurant rent
  • +Parking and car rental
  • −Staff salaries
  • −Aircraft maintenance
  • −Jet fuel
  • −Goods for the shops and restaurants
  • −Food, drinks and supplies for the cabins
  • Pay every salary, from the pilots to the cleaners
  • Keep your aircraft maintained and safe to fly
  • Buy jet fuel, and goods to keep the terminal’s shops and restaurants stocked
  • Load the cabins with food, drinks and supplies before every flight
  • …and much more

Your own phone and computer

In the game you carry a smartphone and work at a computer, each with a fully built operating system and its own apps. This is the phone from the game: tap the apps and try it. The computer is just below.

  • Two bank accounts: your own, where your salary comes in, and the airport’s, with every in and out
  • Mail and messages from your staff, the airlines and the town
  • Hire staff, order supplies and plan timetables from your desk or your pocket
  • The news, and a map of the whole world
  • …and much more

Your office

Your computer. Every window at once.

On the desk in your office stands your computer. It runs the same apps as your phone, with room for many windows side by side, and what you do on one is on the other.

  • Mail from the airlines, your staff, the bank and your family, with folders, stars and replies
  • A calendar for the days you need to remember: on the day, the game reminds you
  • The bank: the airport’s account with every in and out, loans, and accounts of your own for savings or a maintenance reserve
  • Markets for jet fuel, spare parts, and food and drink, and the aircraft market
  • Your photos, videos and documents, the ranking and your career
  • A web browser with real web pages, right inside the game
  • …and much more

Try it: drag a window by its title bar, use the buttons in its corner to minimise, maximise or close it, and click its icon in the taskbar to bring it back.

Under the hood

Unreal Engine 5. AAA graphics.

Airport Dynasty Pro is built for a AAA look, on the same engine the biggest games and films use. Two of its features shape how the game looks and runs; the rest of the picture is below.

Closer = more triangles drawn. Further = fewer. Always just enough.

Nanite

The look
Buildings, aircraft and every bench are made of millions of tiny triangles, film-quality detail. Edges stay round, surfaces stay sharp, from across the apron or a metre away, with no models popping in and out as you move.
Performance
Nanite only draws the detail your screen can actually show and streams the rest as needed. So more detail costs far less than it used to: a huge, detailed airport runs smoothly instead of grinding your PC down.

Move the sun: the light, the glass and the shadows follow.

Lumen

The look
Light bounces like real light: sunshine off the floor, through the glass, onto the people. Nothing is painted on in advance, so dawn, sunsets, storms and night shifts all light up the airport the way they would in life, as the sun moves.
Performance
Real-time light is the most demanding part of the picture, so it scales: the graphics settings let you choose its quality, from lighter on older PCs to full quality on strong ones, and the game checks your PC to suggest a starting point.
  • Virtual Shadow MapsCrisp, soft shadows on every detail, from the tail fins to a coffee cup
  • Glass and reflectionsThe terminal’s glass walls reflect the apron, the sky and the people
  • MetaHumansFaces, skin, hair and movement that look like real people
  • Weather and skyClouds, rain, snow, fog and lightning, lit by the real sun
  • Temporal Super ResolutionSharp 4K-like pictures at higher frame rates
  • And much moreMore graphics features arrive with every update

Every graphics feature has its own setting, so the game looks its best on your PC.
